chosen_angle.working_h1: The Senior Developer Paradox: Why AI Coding Tools Make Seniors Faster but Juniors Slower
chosen_angle.alt_h1: AI Coding Assistants: The Experience-Dependent Productivity Split
chosen_angle.thesis: AI coding assistants have achieved widespread adoption but their productivity impact is not uniformly positive — it strongly correlates with developer experience. Senior developers leverage these tools effectively through superior code review capabilities and contextual understanding, while juniors often experience net slowdown due to increased verification overhead and limited ability to discern subtle flaws in AI output. This experience gradient creates a bifurcated landscape where the same tool that empowers senior engineers to ship 2.5x more AI-generated code simultaneously contributes to junior developers feeling faster while being objectively slower, fundamentally altering senior roles from code authors to verification architects.
chosen_angle.audience: Senior/staff software engineers (8+ years) evaluating AI tooling ROI; engineering leads setting team adoption strategy; technology decision-makers assessing organizational impact
chosen_angle.rationale: Highest composite score on search intent (senior devs actively researching whether AI tools help them specifically), novelty (the experience-dependent productivity split is the most differentiated and actionable finding in the corpus), and taxonomy alignment (perfect fit for senior-dev-focused technical publications). The paradox framework creates immediate narrative tension and allows every section to ladder back to the experience variable as the key moderator.

contradictions_resolved.description: C2 shows seniors slower with AI despite feeling faster; C7 shows seniors ship more AI code than juniors
contradictions_resolved.resolution: Experience gradient explains both: seniors' superior review lets them leverage AI output effectively (more shipped code) but they spend significant time verifying (slower net on complex tasks); juniors lack review skills so they neither leverage nor verify effectively (feel faster due to generation speed but ship less and may miss errors)
